automated_invention_candidate.target_constraint: Must withstand 100,000 thermal cycles at temperatures up to 1200°C without crack initiation
automated_invention_candidate.observed_phenomenon: Thermal barrier coatings (TBCs) reduce substrate temperature in high-temperature applications
source_mechanisms: Ceramic coatings with low thermal conductivity create temperature gradient across coating thickness

exact_evidence_spans.span_text: Yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) coatings reduced substrate temperature by 100-150°C in laboratory testing

automated_invention_candidate.mechanism: Applying YSZ thermal barrier coating to turbine blade surface reduces metal substrate temperature, extending fatigue life
automated_invention_candidate.cross_domain_connection: Thermal barrier coating mechanism from laboratory specimens transfers to gas turbine blade application
automated_invention_candidate.proposed_intervention: Apply 300-micron YSZ coating via plasma spray to turbine blade airfoil surfaces
automated_invention_candidate.expected_causal_effect: Coating creates 100°C temperature drop across coating thickness, reducing substrate temperature from 1100°C to 1000°C, extending fatigue life by factor of 3
automated_invention_candidate.falsification_test: Run thermal cycling test with 300-micron YSZ coating; if substrate temperature reduction is less than 50°C or if coating spalls before 10,000 cycles, hypothesis is falsified

unsupported_assumptions.evidence_gap: No substrate specification in candidate or source evidence

unsupported_assumptions.reason_unsupported: Coating process affects microstructure and properties. Candidate mentions 'plasma spray' but provides no microstructural details.
unsupported_assumptions.impact: Porosity level strongly affects thermal conductivity. 5-15% porosity variation could change thermal conductivity by factor of 2.
unsupported_assumptions.evidence_gap: No coating process parameters or microstructural characterization in evidence

simulation_request.blocking_reason: Request contains 3 unsupported assumptions not grounded in candidate evidence: (1) YSZ thermal conductivity assumed from literature rather than measured/specified, (2) substrate material arbitrarily chosen as Inconel 718 without candidate specification, (3) coating microstructure/porosity assumed without process parameters. These assumptions introduce unquantified uncertainty that could invalidate simulation predictions. The pipeline must never silently invent physical parameters.

expected_outcome.reason: Simulation request contains material properties and boundary conditions that were invented/assumed rather than derived from candidate evidence. The system correctly identifies these unsupported assumptions and blocks the request to prevent silent parameter invention.
